안녕히 계세요.forms: casual: 잘 있어 · formal: 안녕히 계십시오
안녕히 계세요.x: Thank you for the meal. Goodbye!
안녕히 계세요.e: 안녕히 (peacefully) + 계세요 (please stay) — 'stay in peace'; said by the one leaving.
안녕히 계세요.t: Used when YOU are leaving and the other person stays, e.g. leaving a shop or someone's home.

한국.x: I came to Korea last year.
한국.t: Add 사람 for people (한국 사람) and 어/말 for language (한국어, 한국말).

건강.x: I exercise every day for my health.
건강.t: 건강하세요! ('Stay healthy!') is a common warm goodbye or New Year wish.

가격.x: How much do these sneakers cost?
가격.t: 가격 is a bit more formal than native 값; you'll see it on signs and price tags.

시작하다.t: Pronounced [시자카다]. Works both ways: 수업이 시작해요 / 수업을 시작해요.

예약하다.x: I booked the restaurant for seven in the evening.

구경.ex: 저는 시장에서 이것저것 구경하는 것을 좋아해요.
구경.x: I like looking around at all sorts of things at the market.
구경.e: Think 'browsing': 구경하다 is looking around for fun, not for a purpose.
구경.t: 구경만 할게요 'I'm just looking' is handy when a shop clerk approaches you.

설명.x: I understood after hearing the teacher's explanation.

계약서.x: Read the contract carefully before you sign it.

연장하다.x: I extended my student visa for one more year.
연장하다.t: Common collocations: 비자를 연장하다, 기간을 연장하다, 계약을 연장하다 (extend a contract).

절약하다.m: to save, to economize, to conserve
절약하다.ex: 물을 절약하기 위해 샤워 시간을 줄였어요.
절약하다.x: I cut my shower time to save water.
절약하다.t: Pronounced [저랴카다]; 절약 is using less, while 저축 is putting money away.

긍정적.x: Even when things are hard, I try to think positively.

반응.x: The audience's reaction was very good.
반응.t: Pronounced [바능]: the ㄴ moves over to the next syllable.

대충.x: I didn't have time, so I gave my room a quick, rough cleaning.

옛날 옛적에.forms: set phrase: 옛날 옛적에 … 살았어요 (storytelling style: 살았답니다)
옛날 옛적에.m: once upon a time, long, long ago
옛날 옛적에.ex: 옛날 옛적에 깊은 산속에 호랑이 한 마리가 살았어요.
옛날 옛적에.x: Once upon a time, a tiger lived deep in the mountains.
옛날 옛적에.e: 옛날 'the old days' + 옛적 'olden times' + 에 'at': two near-synonyms stacked for storytelling rhythm.
옛날 옛적에.t: Pronounced [옌날 옏쩌게]: the final ㅅ becomes ㄴ before ㄴ, and ㅈ turns tense after it. Folktales often go on with 호랑이 담배 피우던 시절에 'back when tigers smoked'.

악영향.ex: 잠이 부족하면 건강에 악영향을 줄 수 있어요.
악영향.x: Lack of sleep can have a negative effect on your health.
악영향.t: Pronounced [아경향]: the ㄱ moves over to the next syllable.

인성.x: At school, character education matters as much as grades.
인성.t: Koreans often judge someone with 인성이 좋다/나쁘다 'a good/bad person at heart'.

윷놀이.m: yunnori (traditional board game played with four sticks)
윷놀이.x: I played yunnori with my family on Lunar New Year.
윷놀이.e: 윷 (the four throwing sticks) + 놀이 'game' — a classic Lunar New Year game.
윷놀이.t: Pronounced [윤노리] — the final ㅊ sounds like ㄷ, then becomes ㄴ before ㄴ.

화석 연료.ex: 화석 연료를 많이 쓰면 공기가 나빠져요.
화석 연료.x: Using a lot of fossil fuels makes the air worse.
화석 연료.t: 연료 is pronounced [열료]: ㄴ turns into ㄹ next to ㄹ.

오싹하다.x: Hearing the scary story sent a chill down my spine.
오싹하다.e: From the mimetic 오싹 — the sudden shiver.
오싹하다.t: Works for both cold and fear; 오싹오싹 intensifies it.

구상하다.m: to plan out, to conceive, to envision (an idea or project)
구상하다.ex: 요즘 새 소설의 줄거리를 구상하고 있어요.
구상하다.x: These days I'm working out the plot of a new novel.

지정하다.m: to designate, to appoint, to specify
지정하다.ex: 선생님이 학생들에게 각자 앉을 자리를 지정해 주셨어요.
지정하다.x: The teacher assigned each student a seat.

코앞에 닥치다.m: to be just around the corner, to be imminent (lit. to come right up in front of one's nose)
코앞에 닥치다.ex: 시험이 코앞에 닥쳤는데 아직 공부를 못 했어요.
코앞에 닥치다.x: The exam is right around the corner, and I still haven't studied.
코앞에 닥치다.e: 코앞 'in front of the nose' means very close in space or time; 닥치다 means 'to come upon, to draw near'.
코앞에 닥치다.t: Used for exams, deadlines and events that are worryingly close. 코앞이에요 alone also works: 시험이 코앞이에요.

수익률.x: This fund's rate of return last year was 8 percent.

고립감.x: Living alone abroad, I felt isolated.

관용.ex: 다른 사람의 실수에 관용을 베풀 줄 알아야 해요.
관용.x: You need to know how to show tolerance for other people's mistakes.
관용.t: Homonym: 관용 also means 'customary usage', as in 관용어 (idiom); 관용을 베풀다 = to show tolerance.

투약.x: Medicine must be given to the patient at the set times.
투약.t: 투약 is what medical staff do; the patient's side is 복용 (taking medicine).

진척되다.m: to progress, to move forward (of work or a project)
진척되다.x: The construction is progressing faster than scheduled.
진척되다.t: 진척 is about work getting done (공사, 작업); 진전 suits talks and relations.

오명.ex: 그 회사는 환경 오염 기업이라는 오명을 벗었습니다.
오명.x: The company shed its reputation as a polluter.

지상권.m: surface right, superficies (right to use another's land for buildings or trees)
지상권.ex: 건물 주인은 남의 땅에 대한 지상권을 가지고 있습니다.
지상권.x: The building owner holds a surface right on someone else's land.
지상권.e: Literally 'right above the land' — to build on land you don't own.

분식회계.x: The company inflated its profits through accounting fraud.
분식회계.e: Literally 'powdered-up accounting' — making the books look prettier than they are.
분식회계.t: Unrelated to 분식 'snack food' like 떡볶이, a different word with the same sound.

국교정상화.x: The normalization of diplomatic relations between Korea and Japan took place in 1965.
국교정상화.e: Literally 'making relations between nations normal again'.

유감표명.ex: 상대국은 공식 사과 대신 유감표명만 했습니다.
유감표명.x: The other country only expressed regret instead of making an official apology.
유감표명.t: In diplomacy, 유감 is noticeably weaker than a real 사과 'apology'.

비장.ex: 그 환자는 교통사고로 비장이 파열되어 수술을 받았습니다.
비장.x: The patient had surgery after his spleen ruptured in a car accident.
비장.t: Homonym warning: 비장 also means 'secretly kept', as in 비장의 무기 (secret weapon).

신석기.m: Neolithic stone tools; the Neolithic (New Stone Age)
신석기.ex: 신석기 시대 사람들은 농사를 짓기 시작했어요.
신석기.x: People in the Neolithic era began farming.
신석기.e: Literally 'new stone tools' — polished stone tools.
신석기.t: Watch the pronunciation: 신석기 sounds like [신석끼].

탈상.ex: 요즘은 사십구재를 마치고 탈상하는 경우가 많아요.
탈상.x: These days, many families end mourning after the forty-ninth-day rite.
탈상.e: Literally 'taking off mourning' — once meant removing mourning clothes after three years.

전전반측.m: tossing and turning, being unable to sleep
전전반측.x: I was so worried about tomorrow's exam that I tossed and turned all night.
전전반측.e: From an ancient Chinese poem: rolling from side to side, unable to sleep.

투영하다.m: to project, to reflect (one's feelings or ideas onto something)
투영하다.x: The author projected his own experiences onto the main character.
투영하다.e: Literally 'throw a shadow' — casting an image onto something.

순응하다.m: to adapt, to conform, to comply
순응하다.x: People live by adapting to new environments.
순응하다.t: 순응 suggests passively going along; 적응 is the neutral word for adjusting.

허상.ex: SNS 속 화려한 삶은 허상일 때가 많아요.
허상.x: The glamorous lives on social media are often an illusion.

고식지계.m: a stopgap measure, a temporary fix
고식지계.ex: 그 정책은 문제를 덮는 고식지계에 불과합니다.
고식지계.x: That policy is nothing more than a stopgap that covers up the problem.
고식지계.e: Literally 'a plan just to rest for now'.
고식지계.t: Often followed by 에 불과하다 'is nothing more than'.

조영제.ex: CT 촬영 전에 조영제 주사를 맞았어요.
조영제.x: I got a contrast dye injection before the CT scan.
조영제.e: Literally 'image-making drug': it makes organs show up on scans.
